Document: Practice Direction 54A – Judicial review
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 18.2 (1) A person who makes an application for permission to apply for judicial review must file a claim form and a copy at court, and the Claim Form must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (a) indicate on its face that this Section of the Practice Direction applies; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (b) be accompanied by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (i) a copy of the removal directions and the decision to which the application relates; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (ii) any document served with the removal directions including any document which contains the UKVI’s factual summary of the case; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (c) contain or be accompanied by a clear and concise statement of the claimant’s grounds for bringing the claim for judicial review; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (d) state the claimant’s Home Office reference number;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] If the claimant is unable to comply with paragraph (b) or (c) or (d) above the Claim Form must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the reasons why. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (2) The claimant must, immediately upon issue of the claim, send copies of the issued Claim Form and accompanying documents to the address specified by the UKVI . [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] ( Rule 54.7 also requires the defendant to be served with the Claim Form within 7 days of the date of issue. Rule 6.10 provides that service on a Government Department must be effected on the solicitor acting for that Department, which in the case of the UKVI is the Government Legal Department (“GLD”). The address for GLD may be found in the Annex to Part 66 of these Rules .)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 18.3 Where the claimant has not complied with paragraph 18.2(1)(b) or (c) or (d) but has provided reasons why he is unable to comply, and the court has issued the Claim Form, the Administrative Court—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (a) will refer the matter to a Judge for consideration as soon as practicable; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (b) will notify the parties that it has done so. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 18.4 If, upon a refusal to grant permission to apply for judicial review, the Court decides that the application is clearly without merit, that decision will be included in the order refusing permission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 19.1 A person who makes an application for permission to apply for judicial review of the decision of the Upper Tribunal refusing permission to appeal must file a Claim Form which must: (a) state on its face that the application is made under Rule 54.7A ; (b) identify which of the categories at Rule 54.7A(1)(a) – (c) apply; and (c) set out succinctly the grounds relied on in support of the claim.
